chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of his companions, from Marwak ibn Ubayd, from Zur'at ibn Muhammad, from Sama'at ibn Mihran, from Abu Baseer, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The woman is favored over the man by ninety-nine parts of pleasure, but Allah has attached shyness to them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between men and women in terms of pleasure and modesty according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the physiological and spiritual distinction between genders, noting that women possess ninety-nine parts of pleasure compared to men's one part. This quantitative superiority is balanced by the divine bestowal of *hayaa* (modesty), which serves as a natural restraint and distinguishing characteristic for women. This concept underscores the Shia view of complementary gender roles, where heightened sensitivity is tempered by innate dignity.
